title: Prefix zipper merge for fragment orthogonalization and slab packing
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Our current prefix fragment storage often leaves orthogonal (non-overlapping) prompt fragments scattered across multiple GPU slabs and KV shards. This increases slab fragmentation, causes redundant KV entries for highly similar prompts, and inflates GPU memory usage and tail latency during continuous batching.

Proposal: Implement a "prefix zipper merge" pass that runs as part of KV ingestion and periodic compaction. The zipper merge detects orthogonal fragment boundaries from recent request windows, interleaves (zips) compatible fragments into compact slab segments, and emits canonicalized fragment identifiers to enable cross-request deduplication. The algorithm focuses on three goals: 1) maximize co-location of re-usable token spans on the same GPU slab, 2) avoid creating long-lived large fragments that block slab reclamation, and 3) preserve O(1) lookup for KV hits during generation.

High-level flow:
- Ingest: when new fragments are produced from batched requests, compute lightweight locality signatures (rolling hash + span length + tenant affinity).
- Candidate selection: identify fragments whose signatures indicate orthogonality (no overlapping token indexes) and similar lifetime estimates (based on request TTL heuristics).
- Zipper merge: interleave token streams from multiple candidates into a packed slab buffer with a small header that stores per-fragment offsets. The header uses a compact delta encoding to keep lookups fast and cache-friendly.
- Emit: write compacted slab to GPU-resident allocator and update prefix registry with a canonicalized compact-id. Old fragments are tombstoned and scheduled for reclamation after safe-grace period.

Why different from previous approaches: instead of global dedupe via content-addressed chunking (expensive and leads to small-chunk overhead) or coarse-grained coalescing (which can block eviction), zipper merge produces medium-grain, orthogonality-aware packing that is friendly to continuous batching and reduces contention on the slab allocator.

Expected benefits: lower GPU memory footprint (target 12-20% reduction for mixed chat workloads), fewer duplicate KV entries across similar prompts, improved tail latency under heavy interleaved batching due to co-located KV hits.

Risks and mitigations: zippering adds CPU compaction work and a metadata header that slightly increases lookup complexity. We'll mitigate via: 1) running compaction on a bounded background worker pool, 2) keeping header format simple for in-GPU lookup kernels, 3) telemetry to abort zippering if it increases p95 latency during rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for zipper merge correctness (reconstruct token spans from packed slab)
Integration test demonstrating canonical id reuse across two simulated interleaved requests
Benchmark showing >=12% GPU memory saving on representative mixed chat workload (local cluster sim) or no regression on short-sequence workloads
End-to-end A/B on staging with rollout flag: no more than 2% increase in p50/p95 generation latency during warmup window; p95 improved by target on heavy interleaved batches
Eviction and reclamation flow verified: tombstoned fragments reclaimed within configured grace period without KV lookup failures
implementation_notes: Add a compact header format (delta-encoded offsets + 8-bit ttl bucket) that fits 64B cache lines for fast kernel reads
New background compactor service (configurable concurrency) that pulls candidate fragments from recent-window index
Extend prefix registry API with 'canonical_compact_id' and 'tombstone_ts' fields (string ids and timestamps stored in registry)
Safe rollout behind runtime flag 'kv.zipper_merge.enabled' with per-tenant opt-out for initial canary
Metric instrumentation: zipper.compactions_total, zipper.compaction_failed, zipper.avg_pack_ratio, zipper.cpu_ms_per_compaction
Local repro harness in tools/kv-sim to measure pack_ratio and memory serving impact; scripts for synthetic workload generation included
Ensure GPU kernel lookup supports two-level mapping: compact_id -> base_offset + per-fragment delta; fallback to original fragment lookup on mismatch
comments: 2026-03-04 - Sofia Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes attached to confluence doc. Decided to prefer delta-encoded headers vs per-fragment absolute offsets to reduce header size.

2026-03-06 - Ethan Wang: Prototype zipper pass implemented in branch runtime/zipper-proto. Early microbench shows pack_ratio ~1.6x for synthetic interleaved prompts (good), CPU cost ~2.3ms/compaction per fragment set on dev VM.
2026-03-08 - Priya Kapoor (Performance): Reviewed prototype. Suggested adding ttl-bucket heuristics to avoid zippering fragments that are likely single-use (system prompts, ephemeral traces).
2026-03-09 - QA: Added integration test scaffolding. Found edge case where packing >1k fragments caused header overflow; limiting candidates per-compact run to 256 fixes it.
2026-03-10 - Security Review: Header format contains only offsets and ttl-bucket; no PII. No extra review required, but ensure logging doesn't include full prompt content.

2026-03-12 - Ethan Wang: Staging A/B started with 10% tenant sample. Observed 14% GPU memory reduction in the sample but CPU compaction spikes on certain tails. Tuning background pool to 4 workers reduced spikes.
2026-03-13 - Sofia Martinez: Plan for next week: add dynamic admission control that disables zippering when compactor CPU > threshold for >10s; prepare canary checklist for production rollouts.
